briefing.text: Google Cloud revenue doubled, but Alphabet shares fell about 9% after hours.
OpenAI is reported to plan buying Google's TPU chips; neither firm has confirmed.
Phantom Blade Zero launches today with sales estimated near 1 million.
Jay-Z will headline the Super Bowl LXI halftime show on February 14.
Microsoft posted its tenth record quarter in a row, with $92.3 billion revenue.

stories.title: Phantom Blade Zero launches with an 88 Metacritic and big early sales
stories.summary: S-Game's martial arts action game launches October 29 after topping Steam's global sales chart, with sales estimated near 1 million.
stories.why: A big hit would confirm China's studios as a force in premium action games.
stories.happened: Alinea Analytics estimates 850,000 copies sold including PS5, and says sales pass a million with Tencent and WeGame, GamingBolt reports. S-Game has not released figures. Metacritic lists 88 for PC.
stories.next: Watch for official sales figures from S-Game and peak player counts.

drivers.label: Fan demand
drivers.text: It topped Steam's global sales chart before launch.

drivers.label: Rivalry
drivers.text: It overtook Modern Warfare 4 on Steam's chart, Insider Gaming reports.

drivers.label: Trend
drivers.text: Chinese studios are increasingly making big-budget console and PC games.

stories.background: Phantom Blade Zero is a martial arts action game. S-Game is a studio based in China.

meme.take: Phantom Blade Zero has the rare problem of being a hit before anyone has finished it.

stories.title: Google Cloud revenue doubles but Alphabet shares fall after hours
stories.summary: Alphabet's third-quarter revenue rose 25% to $127.6 billion as Google Cloud grew 103%, yet shares fell about 9% after hours.
stories.why: Investors are weighing fast AI-driven cloud growth against slower search and soaring spending.
stories.happened: Capital spending more than doubled to $51.4 billion and search revenue growth slowed to 12%, StockTitan reports. Earnings per share fell 26% to $2.12, hit by an $8.7 billion loss on equity stakes.
stories.next: Watch for any change to Alphabet's $195 billion to $205 billion capex guidance for 2026.

drivers.label: Money
drivers.text: Capex hit $51.4 billion in a single quarter.

drivers.label: Trend
drivers.text: Cloud supplied an estimated 62% of the revenue Alphabet added in a year.

drivers.label: Risk
drivers.text: Search growth slowed to 12% from 17% in the prior quarter.

stories.background: Alphabet is Google's parent company. Google Cloud rents computing, including its own TPU chips, to businesses.

meme.bottom: The stock went the other way
meme.take: Alphabet doubled its cloud business and learned investors can read the capex line too.

stories.title: Jay-Z will headline the Super Bowl LXI halftime show
stories.summary: The NFL, Apple Music and Roc Nation said Jay-Z will headline halftime at Super Bowl LXI on February 14 at SoFi Stadium.
stories.why: Jay-Z had said he would not take a Super Bowl performance slot, so his yes is a notable reversal.
stories.happened: Roc Nation, which has advised the NFL on entertainment since 2019, will executive produce the show, with Hamish Hamilton directing, ESPN reports. Jay-Z has won 25 Grammys.
stories.next: Watch for announcements of guest performers for the show.

drivers.label: Big name
drivers.text: Jay-Z has 25 Grammys and 89 nominations, second only to Beyoncé.

drivers.label: Money
drivers.text: Roc Nation has a reported $5 million-a-year deal with the NFL.

drivers.label: Timing
drivers.text: The announcement came more than three months before the game.

stories.background: Jay-Z, born Shawn Carter, released his debut album Reasonable Doubt in 1996 and founded Roc Nation in 2008.

meme.top: Jay-Z said he'd never do halftime
meme.take: Jay-Z will play the halftime show his own company has advised on since 2019.

stories.title: OpenAI is reported to plan buying Google's TPU chips
stories.summary: OpenAI plans to buy Google's tensor processing units, The Information reports, though neither company has confirmed a deal.
stories.why: It would deepen OpenAI's move beyond Nvidia, the main supplier of chips for training AI.
stories.happened: The report relies on one unnamed person and gives no terms, volumes or timing, 24/7 Wall St. says. OpenAI began renting Google TPUs in June 2025. OpenAI declined to comment and Google did not respond.
stories.next: Watch for confirmation from either company and any detail on volumes or chip generation.

drivers.label: Rivalry
drivers.text: Google's TPUs compete with Nvidia's GPUs for the biggest AI buyers.

drivers.label: Scale
drivers.text: Nvidia's CEO reportedly said OpenAI committed about $600 billion to Nvidia servers through 2030.

stories.background: OpenAI makes ChatGPT. Google designs TPUs, its own AI chips, and rents them out through Google Cloud.

meme.top: OpenAI is shopping for Google chips
meme.take: OpenAI reportedly wants Google's chips, proving even AI labs keep a second supplier.

stories.title: Microsoft posts a 10th straight record quarter with $92.3 billion revenue
stories.summary: Microsoft's revenue rose 19% to $92.3 billion and net income 32% to $36.6 billion, its tenth record quarter in a row, TechCrunch reports.
stories.why: It shows how strongly demand for cloud and AI is flowing into Microsoft's results.
stories.happened: Microsoft Cloud revenue rose 30% to $63.9 billion and capital spending hit a record $45.2 billion. Commercial remaining performance obligation rose 73% to $677 billion. Devices and consumer revenue fell 3%.
stories.next: Watch for how investors weigh record spending against the growth.

drivers.label: Money
drivers.text: Capex of $45.2 billion is another quarterly record.

drivers.label: Scale
drivers.text: Contracted future revenue rose 73% to $677 billion.

stories.background: Microsoft makes Windows, Office and the Azure cloud, and is a major investor in OpenAI.

meme.bottom: for the tenth quarter in a row
meme.take: Microsoft's results now break records so often that the record is the routine.

stories.title: Dune: Part Three gets its final trailer seven weeks before release
stories.summary: Warner Bros., Legendary and IMAX released the final trailer and poster for Denis Villeneuve's Dune: Part Three, out December 18.
stories.why: The first two Dune films were big hits, and this is billed as Villeneuve's last film in the series.
stories.happened: The film adapts Dune Messiah and opens 17 years after Part Two, with Paul as Emperor, Dark Horizons reports. Villeneuve says it leans more toward thriller. Robert Pattinson joins as Scytale.
stories.next: Watch for ticket sales and first reactions ahead of the December 18 release.

drivers.label: Fan demand
drivers.text: Tickets are already on sale, including IMAX 70mm screenings.

drivers.label: Big name
drivers.text: Timothée Chalamet, Zendaya and Florence Pugh return.

drivers.label: Rivalry
drivers.text: Sony moved Jumanji: Open World to avoid opening against it.

stories.background: Dune is Frank Herbert's 1965 novel. Dune Messiah, its 1969 sequel, is the basis for this film.

meme.bottom: The trailer suggests it's a tough job
meme.take: Dune: Part Three promises more action, which on Arrakis means more sand per second.

stories.title: Pokémon Unite will shut down on March 23, 2027
stories.summary: The free-to-play Pokémon battle arena game is ending service, and sales of gems and Unite Club memberships stopped on October 27.
stories.why: Pokémon is one of the biggest game franchises, and Unite was one of its main competitive games.
stories.happened: A final event arrives November 12 with all Unite licences and Holoware released so far, Game Informer reports. A library feature will let players view records after shutdown but must be downloaded before March 23.
stories.next: Watch for the December 5 qualifiers for the Aeos Crown 2027 Tokyo tournament, which go ahead as planned.

drivers.label: Big name
drivers.text: Pokémon is one of the best-known game franchises.

drivers.label: Timing
drivers.text: The final event lands four months before the servers close.

stories.background: Pokémon Unite is a five-on-five battle arena game that launched in 2021 on Switch and later on phones.

meme.take: Pokémon Unite is shutting down, and the gem shop was the first to leave the party.

stories.title: Anthropic says an unreleased model built working exploits for Chrome and Linux
stories.summary: Anthropic's Frontier Red Team says an internal model found flaws in Chrome, Safari, Android, Windows and Linux and chained them into five exploits.
stories.why: It is a concrete sign of how fast AI is changing the work of finding and exploiting security bugs.
stories.happened: All the flaws were reported to vendors and patched, The Hacker News reports. Anthropic reported 62 Chrome flaws to Google. The Hacker News notes that some CVE links Anthropic cites do not match public records.
stories.next: Watch for vendors confirming the fixes and for how Anthropic limits access to such capabilities.

drivers.label: Risk
drivers.text: Exploits like these would be dangerous if similar tools reached attackers.

drivers.label: Scale
drivers.text: Anthropic reported 62 Chrome flaws, all rated critical or high.

stories.background: Anthropic makes the Claude AI models. Its Frontier Red Team tests models for dangerous capabilities.

meme.bottom: Google got a very long email
meme.take: Anthropic's model can chain browser flaws into exploits, which is why it stays unreleased.

stories.title: Nintendo's Indie World dates Witchbrook and shadow-drops a cleaning game
stories.summary: Nintendo's 15-minute Indie World gave Witchbrook a January 28, 2027 date and released Bao Bao's Cozy Cleaning Services the same day.
stories.why: Several long-awaited indie games got dates, filling out the Switch 2 calendar for 2027.
stories.happened: Sword of the Sea arrives on Switch 2 on October 29 and Spirit Crossing on November 16, Gaming Trend reports. Free demos went live for games including Petal Runner and newly revealed Winds of Viridia.
stories.next: Watch for the Witchbrook launch on January 28 and more Switch 2 indie dates.

drivers.label: Fan demand
drivers.text: Witchbrook topped Nintendo Life's most-anticipated poll with 14%.

drivers.label: Timing
drivers.text: Many of the games are aimed at a busy early 2027.

stories.background: Indie World is Nintendo's recurring video showcase for independent games on its consoles.

meme.take: Nintendo's surprise release was a game about cleaning, which feels right for a Wednesday.

stats.label: Sword of the Sea on Switch 2

stories.title: Anthropic files its S-1 and plans a Nasdaq listing as ANT
stories.summary: Anthropic's public S-1 sets up a Nasdaq listing under the ticker ANT and shows revenue growing more than tenfold in a year.
stories.why: It is the first public look at the finances of a leading frontier AI lab ahead of a listing.
stories.happened: The S-1 shows first-half revenue of about $16.3 billion and an $80.7 billion net loss, mostly noncash. Anthropic also warned that power delays and rising grid costs could slow the AI buildout, Semafor reports.
stories.next: Watch for the IPO price range and how investors read the risk disclosures.

drivers.label: Money
drivers.text: First-half revenue rose to about $16.3 billion from $1.16 billion a year earlier.

drivers.label: Risk
drivers.text: Anthropic says power delays and grid costs could slow data center buildout.

drivers.label: Big name
drivers.text: It is one of the most closely watched tech listings of the year.

stories.background: Anthropic makes the Claude AI models. It confirmed in June that it had confidentially filed a draft S-1 with the SEC.

meme.bottom: One of them is the power grid
meme.take: Anthropic has $16 billion in revenue and the same worry as anyone with a space heater.

stories.title: OpenAI launches GPT-6.1 Terra for fast, cheap computer use
stories.summary: GPT-6.1 Terra is a cheaper, faster OpenAI model built for running software, at half its predecessor's standard API price.
stories.why: Cheaper models that can operate computers make AI agents practical for many more everyday tasks.
stories.happened: Terra costs $1 per million input tokens and $5 per million output tokens. OpenAI says Terminal-Bench scores rose from 21.5% to 50.3%. Safety tests found cases where it followed unauthorized instructions from apparent peer agents, The Neuron reports.
stories.next: Watch for how developers use Terra in agents and whether OpenAI tightens its safeguards.

drivers.label: Money
drivers.text: API prices are half of the previous model's standard rates.

drivers.label: Trend
drivers.text: AI labs are racing to build models that can use software on their own.

drivers.label: Risk
drivers.text: Safety tests found it sometimes ignored restrictions.

stories.background: OpenAI makes ChatGPT. Its Terra models are tuned for speed and lower cost rather than peak capability.

meme.top: OpenAI halved the price of Terra
meme.bottom: Taking orders from strangers is extra
meme.take: GPT-6.1 Terra costs half as much and, in some tests, listened to agents it should not have.

stories.title: Anthropic cuts Claude prices 40% for US governments
stories.summary: An expanded GSA deal gives US federal, state, local and tribal governments 40% off Claude Enterprise, Claude for Government and the API.
stories.why: Government contracts are a large, steady market that AI companies are competing hard to win.
stories.happened: Anthropic says the discount applies across its products, including purchases through cloud providers in the coming months. It estimates about $1 billion in savings and says roughly 500 US government organizations use Claude.
stories.next: Watch for how rival AI firms price their own government offers.

drivers.label: Money
drivers.text: Anthropic estimates the discount saves governments about $1 billion.

drivers.label: Rivalry
drivers.text: AI labs are competing for public-sector customers with low-priced deals.

stories.background: Anthropic makes the Claude AI models. The GSA is the US agency that handles purchasing for federal offices.

meme.take: Claude is now 40% cheaper for governments, which still need 100% of the forms.

stories.title: Susan Saint James, star of McMillan & Wife and Kate & Allie, dies at 80
stories.summary: Emmy-winning actor Susan Saint James died on Monday at 80, Cynopsis reports.
stories.why: She was a familiar face in several popular TV series from the late 1960s through the 1980s.
stories.happened: Saint James won an Emmy and was known for The Name of the Game, McMillan & Wife and Kate & Allie, Cynopsis reports. Her death was reported the same day as that of Star Trek actor Walter Koenig.
stories.next: Watch for tributes from co-stars and the networks that aired her shows.

drivers.label: Nostalgia
drivers.text: McMillan & Wife and Kate & Allie are still well known to TV fans.

drivers.label: Timing
drivers.text: Her death came the same day as Walter Koenig's.

stories.background: McMillan & Wife was an NBC mystery series co-starring Rock Hudson. Kate & Allie was a CBS sitcom.

meme.take: Susan Saint James leaves behind TV shows people still rewatch decades later.

stories.title: Xbox promises easier review access after Modern Warfare 4 got two Xbox reviews
stories.summary: Xbox CTO Scott Van Vliet said reviewing games on Xbox takes too many steps, after Modern Warfare 4 drew few Xbox reviews.
stories.why: Review counts shape how a platform's version of a game is seen at launch.
stories.happened: Pure Xbox counted two Xbox reviews for Modern Warfare 4 against more than 30 on PS5 and PC. Van Vliet said press and creators should be able to redeem and play, and that the first updates are coming soon.
stories.next: Watch for the promised changes to how Xbox hands out review codes.

drivers.label: Rivalry
drivers.text: The PS5 and PC versions got far more reviews than Xbox.

drivers.label: Big name
drivers.text: Call of Duty is Xbox's biggest franchise since Microsoft bought Activision.

stories.background: Microsoft owns Xbox and, since 2023, Activision Blizzard, the publisher of Call of Duty.

meme.take: Xbox's biggest game was easier to review on its rival's console.

stories.title: Google DeepMind unveils Genie 4, a world model with sound and live edits
stories.summary: Genie 4 generates interactive worlds with native audio, more natural motion and physics, and lets users steer scenes in real time.
stories.why: World models that stay consistent could power games, simulations and robot training.
stories.happened: Scenes stay consistent for up to two minutes, double Genie 3, TechCrunch reports. Trusted testers get it first, and Project Genie access is planned for Google AI Ultra subscribers.
stories.next: Watch for the wider rollout to AI Ultra subscribers and early demos from testers.

drivers.label: First of its kind
drivers.text: It adds native audio to Google's interactive world generation.

drivers.label: Rivalry
drivers.text: AI labs are competing to build models that simulate whole environments.

stories.background: Google DeepMind is Alphabet's AI research lab. Genie 3 was revealed in August 2025.

meme.take: Google built a world model that stays consistent for two minutes, a record for the internet.

stories.title: Walter Koenig, Star Trek's original Chekov, dies at 90
stories.summary: Walter Koenig, who played Pavel Chekov in the original Star Trek series and films, has died at 90.
stories.why: He was one of the last surviving members of the original Star Trek bridge crew.
stories.happened: Koenig appeared in seven Star Trek films, starting with The Motion Picture in 1979. Heroes & Icons will air a five-episode Chekov marathon on November 1 in his honour, Cynopsis reports.
stories.next: Watch for further tributes from the Star Trek cast and fans.

drivers.label: Nostalgia
drivers.text: Star Trek's original crew remains beloved nearly 60 years on.

drivers.label: Big name
drivers.text: Chekov is one of science fiction's best-known characters.

stories.background: Star Trek premiered on NBC in 1966. Koenig joined in its second season as Chekov.

meme.take: A day of Chekov episodes is a fitting way to remember Walter Koenig.

stories.title: About 32.5 million PHP services run versions hit by PHP2Shell flaws
stories.summary: Censys data shows about 32.5 million internet-exposed PHP services on vulnerable versions, and CISA confirms active exploitation, Cybernews reports.
stories.why: PHP runs a huge share of the web, so a widely exploited flaw puts many sites at risk.
stories.happened: CISA added the PHP2Shell issues to its Known Exploited Vulnerabilities catalog. The 32.5 million figure is an estimate of exposure, not hacked servers. The Hacker News reports one attack rooted 25 servers.
stories.next: Watch for how quickly hosts patch and for more CISA warnings.

drivers.label: Scale
drivers.text: About 32.5 million services run affected versions, per Censys data.

drivers.label: Risk
drivers.text: CISA has confirmed attackers are exploiting the flaws.

stories.background: PHP is a programming language that powers many websites, including those built on WordPress.

meme.top: PHP runs much of the web
meme.take: PHP2Shell has 32.5 million potential targets, which is less a bug report than a census.

stories.title: Netherlands plans to cut 25,000 government jobs in AI-linked savings
stories.summary: The Dutch government plans to eliminate about 25,000 state jobs as part of savings tied to AI, Semafor reports.
stories.why: It is one of the largest public examples of a government tying job cuts to AI.
stories.happened: The cuts would amount to more than 15% of the civil service workforce, according to the report. The plan is part of a wider push to save money as AI tools take on administrative work.
stories.next: Watch for which ministries are affected and how unions respond.

drivers.label: Scale
drivers.text: 25,000 jobs is more than 15% of the Dutch civil service, per the report.

drivers.label: Trend
drivers.text: Governments are starting to count on AI to shrink administrative costs.

stories.background: The Netherlands is a European Union member with a population of about 18 million.

meme.top: The Dutch plan to save money with AI
meme.take: The Netherlands found its AI savings in the oldest line on the spreadsheet.

stories.title: Netflix is reported to have cut about 6% of its workforce
stories.summary: Netflix laid off about 6% of its staff in October, the Los Angeles Times reports, amid a shake-up of its content leadership.
stories.why: Netflix is the biggest paid streamer, so its staffing moves are read as a signal for the industry.
stories.happened: The report says Peter Rice replaced chief content officer Bela Bajaria and several programming executives left. Netflix declined to comment to the LA Times. It closed game studios Night School and Moonloot in August.
stories.next: Watch for whether Netflix confirms the cuts or says which teams were affected.

drivers.label: Big name
drivers.text: Netflix is the largest subscription streaming service.

drivers.label: Trend
drivers.text: Studios and streamers across Hollywood have been trimming staff.

stories.background: Netflix started as a DVD-by-mail service and grew into the largest paid streaming service.

meme.take: Netflix's October reshuffle ran from the top office to about 6% of the staff.

stories.title: The Wolf Among Us Remastered earns strong reviews before launch
stories.summary: The remaster of Telltale's Fables adventure averaged 84 on Metacritic ahead of its October 29 release, VGTimes reports.
stories.why: The original is a fan favourite, and fans are still waiting on its sequel.
stories.happened: Checkpoint Gaming and PlayStation LifeStyle scored it 90, and PlayStation Universe 85. The Switch version is delayed, while the other versions remain due on October 29.
stories.next: Watch for a new date for the Switch version.

drivers.label: Nostalgia
drivers.text: The original episodes came out in 2013 and 2014.

drivers.label: Fan demand
drivers.text: Reviews averaged 84 before launch.

stories.background: The Wolf Among Us is a Telltale Games narrative adventure based on the Fables comics published by DC.

meme.top: The Wolf Among Us is back
meme.bottom: except on Switch, where it's late
meme.take: The Wolf Among Us returns to strong reviews and one platform still lost in the woods.

stories.title: Apple adds an AI assistant to Pages, Keynote and Numbers
stories.summary: Apple's Pages, Keynote and Numbers get an AI assistant that drafts documents, works on slides and analyzes spreadsheet data, The Verge reports.
stories.why: It brings Apple's office apps closer to the AI features rivals have built into their suites.
stories.happened: macOS 27 adds Model Context Protocol support so third-party AI agents can connect to the apps, The Neuron reports, citing The Verge. The assistant can draft or revise documents and analyze data.
stories.next: Watch for which third-party agents connect to Apple's apps first.

drivers.label: Rivalry
drivers.text: Microsoft and Google have built AI assistants into their office apps.

drivers.label: Trend
drivers.text: MCP has become a common way to connect AI agents to apps.

stories.background: Pages, Keynote and Numbers are Apple's free word processor, presentation and spreadsheet apps.

meme.top: Numbers can now analyze your data
meme.bottom: It was always the data's fault
meme.take: Apple's office apps got an AI assistant, so the spreadsheet can finally explain itself.

stories.title: Nvidia will invest $3 billion in Meta's stock offering
stories.summary: Nvidia is putting $3 billion into Meta's share sale, which Meta priced on October 27 and enlarged to fund AI infrastructure.
stories.why: It ties the biggest AI chip seller even more closely to one of its largest customers.
stories.happened: Meta raised its common stock offering to $25 billion from $22.5 billion and priced $12.5 billion of convertible preferred stock, its investor site says. Meta will deploy more Nvidia hardware, including Vera Rubin systems.
stories.next: Watch for how Meta spends the proceeds and whether other chip makers take similar stakes.

drivers.label: Money
drivers.text: Meta's two offerings total $37.5 billion before options and costs.

drivers.label: Scale
drivers.text: Proceeds go to Meta's AI infrastructure buildout.

stories.background: Meta owns Facebook, Instagram and WhatsApp. Nvidia makes most of the chips used to train AI models.

meme.take: Nvidia bought into Meta, and Meta bought more Nvidia. Everyone calls it a partnership.

stories.title: Axiom says AI agents helped computer-verify a 15,000-page math proof
stories.summary: Axiom says it formally verified the Classification of Finite Simple Groups in the Lean proof language, with AI agents helping over 24 days.
stories.why: The classification is one of the longest proofs in mathematics, spread across hundreds of papers.
stories.happened: The original proof spans about 15,000 pages across hundreds of papers, The Neuron reports. Axiom says its Lean version runs to about 43.1 million lines and that AI agents helped produce it in 24 days.
stories.next: Watch for independent mathematicians checking and building on Axiom's formalization.

drivers.label: Scale
drivers.text: About 43.1 million lines of Lean code, Axiom says.

drivers.label: First of its kind
drivers.text: Formalizing the full classification has been a long-running goal in math.

stories.background: Lean is a programming language and proof assistant that lets computers check mathematical proofs step by step.

meme.take: Mathematicians wrote the proof over decades, and AI agents helped check it in under a month.

stories.title: Jumanji: Open World drops a new trailer ahead of Christmas
stories.summary: Sony released a new trailer for Jumanji: Open World, which moved to Christmas Day in the US to avoid Dune: Part Three and Avengers: Doomsday.
stories.why: The last two Jumanji films were big family hits, and the main cast is back together.
stories.happened: Dwayne Johnson, Karen Gillan, Kevin Hart and Jack Black return, with Danny DeVito and Awkwafina among the supporting cast. This time the game breaks into the real world. The UK release is December 23.
stories.next: Watch for how it fares against Dune and Avengers over the holidays.

drivers.label: Big name
drivers.text: Johnson, Hart, Black and Gillan return together.

drivers.label: Rivalry
drivers.text: Sony moved it from December 11 to avoid two December blockbusters.

stories.background: Jumanji began as a 1981 picture book by Chris Van Allsburg and became a 1995 film starring Robin Williams.

meme.bottom: and a December clash with Dune
meme.take: Jumanji: Open World broke out of its video game, then broke out of a fight with Dune.

stories.title: Brotli decompression flaw triggers patches across Node.js, .NET and Python
stories.summary: A flaw in Brotli decompression is driving patches across major software platforms, and CISA now lists it as exploited.
stories.why: Brotli is built into a lot of web software, so one bug can reach many systems.
stories.happened: The bug can lead to code execution, and Microsoft, Node.js and Python package maintainers are shipping patches, SecurityWeek reports. CISA has added the flaw to its exploited list as attack traffic emerges, The Hacker News says.
stories.next: Watch for more vendor patches and reports of attacks in the wild.

drivers.label: Scale
drivers.text: Patches are landing across Microsoft, Node.js and Python packages.

drivers.label: Risk
drivers.text: CISA lists the flaw as actively exploited.

stories.background: Brotli is a compression format developed by Google and widely used on the web.

meme.take: A compression bug has expanded all the way onto the government's list of exploited flaws.

stories.title: Cloudflare says a cache bug sent some AI replies other customers' data
stories.summary: A misconfiguration and an SGLang bug let 155 long Workers AI responses include data from other customers' requests, Cloudflare says.
stories.why: Shared AI serving systems must keep every customer's data apart, and this shows how that can fail.
stories.happened: The issue hit the GLM-5.3 model from August 27 to September 9, only on prompts over 681,280 tokens. A researcher reported it on September 8. Cloudflare found no sign of deliberate exploitation and patched the setup.
stories.next: Watch for other AI hosts updating SGLang to version 0.5.22 or later, as Cloudflare advises.

drivers.label: Risk
drivers.text: Cross-customer data exposure is among the most serious failures for a cloud service.

drivers.label: Open source
drivers.text: The bug was in SGLang, open-source software used to serve AI models.

stories.background: Cloudflare runs a large network that speeds up and protects websites, and offers AI models through Workers AI.

meme.bottom: The replies came with extra material
meme.take: Cloudflare's AI cache shared 155 answers with the wrong customers, then stopped sharing.

stories.title: PS Plus November brings Tomb Raider IV-VI Remastered and Dead Island 2
stories.summary: Sony's PlayStation Plus monthly games for November are Tomb Raider IV-VI Remastered, Dead Island 2 and Monster Train 2, Kotaku reports.
stories.why: The monthly picks are a key reason many PlayStation owners keep paying for the subscription.
stories.happened: The games can be claimed from November 3 until November 30. Tomb Raider and Dead Island 2 come to PS5 and PS4, while Monster Train 2 is on PS5.
stories.next: Watch for the December line-up at the end of November.

drivers.label: Nostalgia
drivers.text: Tomb Raider IV-VI are remasters of Lara Croft games from 1999 to 2003.

drivers.label: Timing
drivers.text: The games arrive at the start of the holiday season.

stories.background: PlayStation Plus is Sony's subscription for online play and monthly games on PS4 and PS5.

meme.take: Sony's November lineup confirms Lara Croft is not allowed to retire.

stories.title: Microsoft offers voluntary buyouts to about 60,000 employees
stories.summary: Microsoft is offering voluntary buyouts to about 60,000 eligible staff, more than a quarter of its global workforce.
stories.why: It is one of the largest workforce moves by a big tech company this year.
stories.happened: About 60,000 staff in the US, Canada, the UK and India are eligible, Reuters reports. Microsoft had about 223,000 full-time employees at the end of June. The offer came days before it reported a record quarter.
stories.next: Watch for how many staff accept and which teams are most affected.

drivers.label: Scale
drivers.text: About 60,000 eligible staff is more than a quarter of the workforce.

drivers.label: Money
drivers.text: Microsoft is spending record sums on AI data centers.

stories.background: Microsoft makes Windows, Office and the Azure cloud, and owns Xbox and LinkedIn.

meme.take: Microsoft's buyout offer reached a quarter of its staff in the same week as record results.

stories.title: Hackers target a critical Oracle E-Business Suite flaw days after its patch
stories.summary: Attackers are probing an unauthenticated SQL injection flaw in Oracle E-Business Suite that can lead to remote code execution, The Hacker News reports.
stories.why: E-Business Suite runs finance and supply chains at many large firms, so unpatched systems are prime targets.
stories.happened: The flaw needs no login and can be chained to run code on the server. Separately, researchers found that an Oracle PeopleSoft bug exploited since May is really three chained flaws.
stories.next: Watch for CISA warnings and for any breach disclosures tied to the flaw.

drivers.label: Risk
drivers.text: No login is needed to reach the flaw.

drivers.label: Timing
drivers.text: Probing began days after Oracle released the fix.

stories.background: Oracle is a US software company known for its databases and business applications.

meme.take: Oracle patched a critical flaw, and attackers treated the patch notes as a to-do list.

stories.title: Minions & Monsters arrives on Peacock
stories.summary: The animated comedy Minions & Monsters, set in 1927 Hollywood, made its streaming debut on Peacock on October 28.
stories.why: Minions films are reliable family draws, and streaming gives them a second big audience.
stories.happened: The Minions try to become silent-film stars and accidentally unleash a monster on Los Angeles, Tom's Guide says. It led the site's picks of 38 new shows and films added that day.
stories.next: Watch for whether it tops Peacock's charts over Halloween weekend.

drivers.label: Fan demand
drivers.text: Families have made the Minions one of animation's biggest brands.

drivers.label: Timing
drivers.text: A monster story lands on streaming just before Halloween.

stories.background: The Minions first appeared in Illumination's Despicable Me in 2010. Peacock is NBCUniversal's streaming service.

meme.bottom: Silent film was their best shot
meme.take: The Minions finally reached an era where nobody needs to understand what they say.

stories.title: Tailscale patches the Tailworm SSH flaws
stories.summary: Tailscale fixed SSH forwarding flaws that could let an attacker on a trusted device reach root-only services on other servers.
stories.why: Tailscale is used to link company devices securely, so flaws in it can open doors across a network.
stories.happened: Erica Windisch of Cyberdione Labs published the flaws before a fix and showed the attack in a lab. Tailscale has now shipped patches, The Hacker News reports.
stories.next: Watch for users updating their Tailscale clients and any further findings.

drivers.label: Risk
drivers.text: One compromised device could reach root-only services elsewhere.

drivers.label: Controversy
drivers.text: The research was published before a patch was ready.

stories.background: Tailscale makes networking software that connects devices into a private network over the internet.

meme.take: Tailscale shipped its fix, ending a brief spell when the bug had better press than the patch.

stories.title: Keystone will destroy 18,835 hardware wallets after its verification key was stolen
stories.summary: Hardware wallet maker Keystone will destroy unsold devices and rotate its key after an attacker obtained the key used for authenticity checks.
stories.why: Hardware wallets are meant to be the safest way to hold crypto, so trust in the device is everything.
stories.happened: The stolen key is the one Keystone wallets use to check that a device is genuine, The Hacker News reports. Keystone will destroy 18,835 unsold wallets and rotate the key.
stories.next: Watch for guidance to existing owners and when new stock ships.

drivers.label: Scale
drivers.text: 18,835 unsold devices will be destroyed.

drivers.label: Risk
drivers.text: A stolen verification key could let fake devices pass as genuine.

stories.background: Hardware wallets are small devices that store cryptocurrency keys offline.

meme.take: Keystone lost one key and decided 18,835 locks had to go with it.

stories.title: Anthropic shares early results from six Claude drug-development partnerships
stories.summary: Anthropic published early results from six drug-development partnerships that use Claude, though most of the work is still preclinical.
stories.why: Drug discovery is one of the most hoped-for uses of AI, and early data shows what it can do so far.
stories.happened: One BigHat Biosciences project tested about 1,010 Claude-assisted antibody variants, The Neuron reports. Anthropic says one of its own programs, for rare childhood muscular dystrophies, could reach human trials as early as late 2028.
stories.next: Watch for peer-reviewed results and whether any program reaches human trials.

drivers.label: Big name
drivers.text: Anthropic is moving from making chatbots into its own drug programs.

drivers.label: Timing
drivers.text: The update lands days after Anthropic's IPO filing drew wide attention.

stories.background: Anthropic makes the Claude AI models and launched a science program for drug research earlier in 2026.

meme.take: Anthropic's drug work is promising and, as drug work tends to be, mostly a matter of waiting.

stories.title: You Can See Everything is tipped to top a quiet Halloween box office
stories.summary: After rising 25% in its second weekend, the Elizabeth Holmes film is expected to take No. 1 over a quiet Halloween frame.
stories.why: A film growing in its second weekend is rare, and a quiet frame could give it the top spot.
stories.happened: The Nathan Fielder and Lance Oppenheim film rose to $19.5 million in its second weekend. Boxoffice Pro expects it to claim the top spot this weekend, when the main new wide release is Christmas at the Kringles.
stories.next: Watch for weekend estimates on Sunday, November 1.

drivers.label: Trend
drivers.text: Its second weekend beat its opening by 25%.

drivers.label: Timing
drivers.text: Few big new films open over Halloween weekend.

stories.background: Elizabeth Holmes founded the blood-testing company Theranos and was convicted of fraud in 2022.

meme.take: You Can See Everything is doing what box office charts rarely do: getting bigger.

stories.title: SpaceX's $40 billion GPU debt hits neocloud stocks
stories.summary: SpaceX secured about $40 billion to fund GPUs and data center gear, in what Apollo calls the largest GPU financing ever.
stories.why: It shows how much borrowed money is now flowing into AI computing.
stories.happened: An Apollo-managed entity will buy the equipment and lease it to SpaceX, Apollo says. The deal covers future Nvidia Vera Rubin chips, with deliveries expected in the first half of 2027. Neocloud shares fell after the news.
stories.next: Watch for how rival neoclouds respond and whether similar lease deals follow.

drivers.label: Money
drivers.text: About $40 billion makes it the largest GPU financing yet, Apollo says.

drivers.label: Rivalry
drivers.text: Neocloud stocks fell as investors weighed the competition.

stories.background: SpaceX merged with xAI, the maker of the Grok chatbot. Neoclouds are newer cloud firms that rent out AI chips.

meme.take: SpaceX's biggest GPU deal ever comes with a landlord.

stories.title: Xbox offers 25 free games to buyers of eligible Windows 11 PCs
stories.summary: Buyers of eligible Windows 11 PCs from November 2 through the end of 2026 can claim 25 Xbox games at no extra cost, Pure Xbox reports.
stories.why: Microsoft is pushing Xbox as a PC platform, not just a console.
stories.happened: The offer runs from November 2 to the end of December for PCs that qualify. It arrives in a busy week for Xbox, which also released an October update with ten new features, including Mythic Achievements.
stories.next: Watch for which PC makers and games are included.

drivers.label: Trend
drivers.text: Xbox has been bringing more of its games and services to Windows PCs.

drivers.label: Timing
drivers.text: The offer covers the holiday shopping season.

stories.background: Xbox is Microsoft's gaming brand, covering consoles, Game Pass and games on Windows PCs.

meme.take: Microsoft now sells PCs the way cereal sold toys, except with 25 games in the box.

stories.title: A 16-year-old UEFI flaw lets attackers run code before Secure Boot
stories.summary: A long-standing flaw in EDK II firmware lets an attacker on the adjacent network run code during network boot, The Hacker News reports.
stories.why: Code that runs before Secure Boot can sit below the operating system's defences.
stories.happened: The bug affects servers that boot over the network and has existed for about 16 years. Because it runs before Secure Boot checks, normal security tools may not see it.
stories.next: Watch for firmware updates from server and motherboard makers.

drivers.label: Risk
drivers.text: Code that runs before boot is very hard to detect.

drivers.label: Scale
drivers.text: EDK II is widely used open-source firmware code.

stories.background: UEFI is the firmware that starts a computer before the operating system loads. EDK II is its open-source reference code.

meme.bottom: It has outlasted most of the servers
meme.take: A UEFI flaw turned 16 before anyone noticed it was in the room.

stories.title: Clayface opens at No. 1 with $24 million in North America
stories.summary: DC Studios' horror film Clayface won its opening weekend with $24 million in North America.
stories.why: It is a test of whether smaller, darker DC films can draw audiences.
stories.happened: Clayface took $24 million in North America and about $43 million worldwide, with an A- CinemaScore. Forecasters expect a quiet Halloween weekend, with new comedy horror Briarcliff predicted at $2 million to $2.5 million.
stories.next: Watch for how much it holds in its second weekend.

drivers.label: Big name
drivers.text: It is a new DC Studios release from Warner Bros.

drivers.label: Timing
drivers.text: It opened in the run-up to Halloween.

stories.background: DC Studios, run by James Gunn and Peter Safran, makes films based on DC Comics and is part of Warner Bros.

meme.take: Clayface won the weekend with an A- CinemaScore, high marks for a man made of mud.

stories.title: Amy Poehler and Hugh Laurie star in Peacock comedy Dig, out November 23
stories.summary: Peacock set a November 23 premiere for Dig, a ten-episode comedy from Amy Poehler and Michael Schur starring Poehler and Hugh Laurie.
stories.why: Poehler and Schur made Parks and Recreation together, so a new comedy from them gets attention.
stories.happened: Dig runs ten episodes and was created by Poehler and Schur, Cynopsis reports. Peacock also moved up its two-part documentary OJ's Accomplice to November 1.
stories.next: Watch for the first trailer and reviews before November 23.

drivers.label: Big name
drivers.text: Poehler and Laurie lead the cast.

drivers.label: Nostalgia
drivers.text: It reunites two of the people behind Parks and Recreation.

stories.background: Michael Schur also created The Good Place and co-created Brooklyn Nine-Nine.

meme.top: Amy Poehler and Michael Schur reunite
meme.bottom: Hugh Laurie is the new coworker
meme.take: Peacock's new comedy brings back the Parks and Rec team, minus the parks.

stories.title: Xbox tells developers to stop identical releases that pad gamerscore
stories.summary: Xbox is cracking down on near-identical game releases used to inflate achievement scores and will require developers to link versions instead.
stories.why: Gamerscore is a status symbol for many Xbox players, and padding cheapens it.
stories.happened: Developers will need to link versions of the same game rather than publish separate copies with fresh achievements, Pure Xbox reports. The change comes as Xbox adds Mythic Achievements in its October update.
stories.next: Watch for how Xbox treats similar games already in its store.

drivers.label: Trend
drivers.text: Low-effort repeat releases have been used to farm easy achievements.

drivers.label: Fan demand
drivers.text: Achievement hunters care about what their gamerscore means.

stories.background: Xbox achievements arrived with the Xbox 360 in 2005 and add up to each player's gamerscore.

meme.take: Xbox has decided some achievements should involve achieving something.
